correctness.rationale: For finite simple unweighted two-terminal internally disjoint paths, edge gradients are exactly edge vectors whose path sums agree. Orthogonal least squares forces a common corrected path sum weighted by 1/ell_i; the explicitly derived matrix has negative same-path off-diagonal entries and positive cross-path entries. Its maximal absolute row sum is max_i[2-2/ell_i +(2+(r-2)ell_i)/(ell_i^2 sum_j 1/ell_j)], attained by the signs of a row. Cauchy--Schwarz sum_{j != i}1/ell_j >= (r-1)^2/(N-ell_i) gives an all-profile upper bound 3+0.5 sqrt(N/s); one path of length s plus balanced long paths gives 1/(2sqrt(s)) in the limit for every sufficiently large edge count. Independently reconstructed exact rational incidence-Gram projections for (1,2),(1,2,3),(2,2,3),(1,3,4,5),(2,4,5), agreeing with the formula. Code and finite samples corroborate; they are not the proof of the asymptotic quantifier.
